excerpt: CSS has wanted a parent selector for as long as I've written CSS. Shaun Inman proposed qualified selectors in 2008 and Dave Hyatt shot it down on dynamics: "just not functioning in dynamic contexts... or on particularly large sample sets". Firefox has bug 418039 open since 2008. Snook declared it impossible-ish in 2010. Fourteen years of "too slow". Then WebKit shipped it. Safari 15.4 shipped :has() first, this March, and Chrome's Intent to Ship targets 105. Today you can play with it in Canary behind the Experimental Web Platform Features flag. Strange timeline, I'll take it.
title: The :has() heist
